chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I said to him: A man left behind a daughter and a sister (through both parents). He said: 'All the wealth belongs to the daughter, and the sister gets nothing from the father and mother.'

key_terms.لِأَبِيهِ وَأُمِّهِ: from his father and mother (full sister)

ai.seo_question: Who inherits the entire estate when a deceased leaves a daughter and a sister?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq clarifies the principle of 'blocking' (hajb) in Shia inheritance jurisprudence, where the presence of a daughter excludes the sister from both parents (al-khata) entirely, rather than sharing the estate. This ruling underscores the hierarchical precedence of direct descendants over collateral relatives, a key distinction in the Usuli school's interpretation of the Quranic verses. The hadith serves as a practical application of the general rule that closer kinship ties supersede more distant ones in the distribution of the deceased's wealth.
